16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T498,Assuming a fixed BPE vocabulary, the method leverages the fact that many tokens can be split into equivalent subtokens along the BPE merge path.
- CANON: standard training/testing with canonical tokenization.
- STOCHASTOK: randomly split tokens into equivalent subtokens with some probability; simple but distributionally biased over the space of valid tokenizations.
- STOCHASTOK-UNI: condition on a per-token split count and sample uniformly among valid tokenizations under that constraint, reducing bias and increasing support.
- UNIFORM-K: condition on a global total number of splits K and sample uniformly, giving explicit control over perturbation strength.
They evaluate stochastic tokenization injected at different stages (pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and in-context usage) and under two threat models: random non-canonical tokenizations vs worst-case adversarial tokenizations. Theoretical discussion connects training under a tokenization distribution (expected risk) to smoother behavior over tokenization-induced perturbations, while emphasizing that robustness depends on coverage/support alignment between training-time sampling and attack-time search.18:Tb53,整套方案由三部分组成：SigLIP-VQ tokenizer、16B MoE dLLM backbone、Diffusion Decoder。

先看 tokenizer。作者没有沿用传统重建导向的 VQ，而是提出 SigLIP-VQ，把连续视觉输入离散成“fully semantic discrete tokens”。这里的关键不是单纯做更好的压缩，而是让 token 更接近语义单元，能被语言式 backbone 直接消费。传统 VQ token 往往偏局部纹理和重建细节，适合生成但不利于理解；如果压缩率再高一些，生成也会受损。SigLIP-VQ 试图在语义保真和离散统一格式之间找到平衡，使视觉 token 既能支持问答推理，又能作为后续图像生成的中间表示。

再看 backbone。LLaDA2.0-Uni 以 LLaDA2.0 的 16B MoE dLLM 为核心，不走 next-token AR，而是对文本和图像 token 统一采用 block-level masked diffusion。这里的 block-wise mask prediction 很重要。它不是逐 token 自回归，也不是完全无结构地全局去噪，而是在块级别进行掩码和恢复，兼顾并行解码效率与上下文建模能力。作者强调 modality-agnostic MoE，说明专家路由不是按模态硬切，而是让文本和视觉 token 在共享 backbone 中竞争专家容量，这对统一表示学习是更激进的设计。

第三部分是 diffusion decoder。由于 backbone 输出的是语义离散视觉 token，而不是可直接还原高保真图像的重建 token，因此需要一个专门 decoder 把这些 token 转成图像。这个 decoder 经过蒸馏后只需 8 步推理，目的是把统一建模和高质量生成拆成两个相对独立的问题：前者由 dLLM 解决，后者由 decoder 解决。相比把所有视觉细节都塞进统一 backbone，这样更符合容量分工，也更容易扩展到高分辨率生成。

训练上，论文提到 carefully curated large-scale data 和 tailored multi-stage pipeline。虽然你给出的正文片段没有完整展开各阶段细节，但从架构逻辑推断，至少包含：语义视觉 tokenizer 训练、统一多模态 dLLM 训练、decoder 蒸馏与对齐，以及理解/生成混合数据的阶段化配比。这里真正值得注意的是目标函数统一：文本和视觉都在 backbone 中用共享的 masked diffusion objective，而不是像很多混合系统那样文本用 AR、图像用 diffusion，再靠 loss balancing 勉强拼接。作者明确把“单一目标”视为训练稳定性和统一性的来源。

推理优化方面，作者做了两件事。其一是 backbone 的 prefix-aware decoding 优化，用来减少 masked diffusion 文本生成时对已知前缀的重复计算和不必要更新。其二是 decoder 的 few-step distillation，把图像重建压到 8 步。这说明他们知道 unified diffusion 的主要质疑之一就是推理成本，因此在系统层面做了补偿，而不是只强调并行解码的理论优势。19:T47f,This is important for pretraining research for several reasons. First, it pushes the non-AR foundation-model direction seriously, with diffusion used in the backbone itself rather than only as an image decoder. Text and vision are both modeled under a shared block-wise masked diffusion objective. Second, it puts the tokenizer back at the center of unified modeling. The paper’s diagnosis is that earlier unified diffusion models underperformed largely because their discrete visual tokens were not semantic enough, so both understanding and generation suffered. Third, it proposes a clean division of labor: semantic discrete tokens for unified reasoning, and a separate diffusion decoder for high-fidelity image synthesis. That separation between semantic modeling and pixel-level reconstruction is a useful design pattern for future multimodal pretraining. Finally, it directly engages with a key question beyond next-token prediction: whether text must be modeled autoregressively. The answer here is not a naive rejection of AR, but an attempt to make masked diffusion viable for open-ended text through architectural and inference-side fixes.1a:Tafe,The system has three main components: a SigLIP-VQ tokenizer, a 16B MoE diffusion LLM backbone, and a diffusion decoder.

The tokenizer is central. Instead of a standard reconstruction-driven VQ tokenizer, the paper introduces SigLIP-VQ to convert continuous visual inputs into fully semantic discrete tokens. The goal is not just compression, but semantic usability. Traditional VQ tokens often preserve local texture and reconstruction detail, which can help generation but are weak for understanding; stronger compression then hurts generation as well. SigLIP-VQ is designed to produce discrete visual units that are useful for reasoning while still serving as an intermediate representation for image synthesis.

The backbone is built on LLaDA2.0, a 16B MoE discrete diffusion language model. Rather than next-token prediction, it uses a shared block-level masked diffusion objective over both text and image tokens. The block-wise design matters. It is not token-by-token autoregression, but it is also not an unstructured fully bidirectional denoising process. It aims to balance parallel decoding efficiency with stronger contextual modeling. The paper also emphasizes modality-agnostic MoE routing, suggesting that experts are shared across text and vision instead of being hard-partitioned by modality. That is a stronger form of unification than simply concatenating modalities into one sequence.

The third component is a diffusion decoder. Because the backbone predicts semantic discrete visual tokens rather than reconstruction-ready image codes, a dedicated decoder is needed to turn those tokens into high-fidelity images. This decoder is distilled to run in only 8 inference steps. Architecturally, this is a clean decomposition: the dLLM handles unified semantic modeling, while the decoder handles visual detail synthesis. Compared with forcing the backbone to carry all low-level image detail, this is a more scalable allocation of capacity.

Training is described as a curated large-scale, multi-stage pipeline. The excerpt here does not include all stage details, but the likely structure includes tokenizer training, unified multimodal dLLM training, decoder distillation, and staged mixing of understanding and generation data. The key point is objective unification: both text and vision are optimized in the backbone with the same masked diffusion objective, instead of using AR for text and diffusion for images and then balancing heterogeneous losses.

On inference, the paper adds two practical optimizations. First, prefix-aware decoding reduces redundant updates and recomputation for conditioned generation in the backbone. Second, few-step distillation compresses the decoder to 8 steps. This matters because inference cost is one of the main objections to unified diffusion systems.1b:T7e9,The empirical story has three parts: understanding, generation, and unified capability. On understanding benchmarks, LLaDA2.0-Uni is reported to be competitive with specialized VLMs, including strong baselines such as Qwen2.5-VL, which is important because many unified models become generation-heavy and underperform on open-ended visual reasoning. On the generation side, the model supports text-to-image synthesis and instruction-based image editing, with examples such as editing text on a blackboard and generating high-resolution images. This suggests that the semantic-token-plus-decoder design does not collapse generation quality. The most distinctive capability is interleaved generation and reasoning: the model can process and produce text and image tokens within one native framework, which is exactly the kind of behavior unified architectures are supposed to enable.

The hard facts visible from the provided content are that the backbone is a 16B MoE dLLM, the decoder is distilled to 8 steps, and image generation examples include at least 768×1024 resolution. The paper also claims inference gains beyond naive parallel decoding, implying that prefix-aware optimization improves actual wall-clock behavior. The full paper likely contains comparisons against MMaDA, Lumina-DiMOO, Janus, OmniGen2, and other unified systems, along with ablations on tokenizer design, decoder distillation, fixed-length versus open-length generation, and efficiency. The numbers worth checking carefully are: tokenizer codebook size and compression ratio, total multimodal training scale and the understanding/generation data mix, the gap to specialized VLMs on understanding benchmarks, generation metrics or human evaluations, and the latency reduction from prefix-aware decoding plus the 8-step decoder.

If these results hold, the main contribution is not a single best score, but evidence that a discrete diffusion backbone can be a serious unified multimodal foundation-model route rather than a niche alternative to AR.1c:T781,Start from the authors’ failure analysis, then see how each module addresses one failure mode. The main thing worth probing more deeply is whether the classifier is learning content quality itself or partially exploiting formatting priors from anchor datasets such as Wikipedia structure or SFT-style dialogue templates.20:T4ad,StoSignSGD replaces the deterministic sign(g) with a stochastic, structurally designed sign operator whose update is unbiased in expectation. The randomness is not i.i.d. noise; it is adapted along the trajectory using a tracked maximum of historical gradients, so that in expectation the method behaves like a preconditioned SGD step while still emitting ±1 per coordinate (preserving 1-bit communication and numerical robustness).

The theory is presented in two regimes:
- Online/convex optimization: the stochastic sign construction fixes the known non-convergence of SignSGD on non-smooth convex problems and achieves a sharp rate matching the lower bound.
- Non-convex optimization: the paper introduces refined stationarity measures that work under arbitrary norms (to better match problem geometry) and derives a sharp complexity bound claimed to avoid explicit dependence on dimension d, improving prior results by a factor on the order of d√d.

A complementary “unbiased sign conversion” framework is proposed to transform a standard optimizer into an unbiased sign-based counterpart, used to interpret StoSignSGD and to structure ablations around which ingredients are essential.21:T423,LoopLM reuses a stack of L transformer layers for t recurrent steps (shared weights), effectively deepening the computation graph without increasing parameter count. A prediction head is attached at each step, enabling multi-step supervision.

Adaptive compute is implemented via a learned early-exit (or equivalently, a learned weighting over step-wise losses). The key training issue is collapse: without constraints, the model either exits too early (cheap but weak) or always runs the maximum steps (strong but no adaptivity). The proposed fix is an entropy-regularized objective with a uniform prior over exit steps to force unbiased exploration of depths early in training, followed by a focused stage that tunes the compute–quality trade-off and lets the model allocate steps based on input difficulty.

For interpretation, the paper positions recurrence as iterative refinement in latent space, and backs it with controlled studies that aim to disentangle “knowledge storage” from “knowledge manipulation” (composition, multi-hop reasoning).22:T52e,Scale: pretraining up to 7.7T tokens; open-sourced Ouro models at 1.4B and 2.6B parameters.

Efficiency claim: 1.4B/2.6B LoopLMs reportedly match roughly 4B/8B standard (non-looped) transformers on many benchmarks, implying ~2–3× parameter efficiency under their evaluation protocol.

Ablations: varying loop steps shows generally increasing capability with more steps, but training can be unstable due to exit-policy collapse; entropy regularization plus the two-stage schedule stabilizes depth usage and preserves peak performance while enabling early exit on easier inputs.

Mechanistic results: the paper reports similar “knowledge storage density” between looped and non-looped models (on the order of ~2 bits/parameter), while showing larger gains on tasks requiring fact composition and multi-hop reasoning—supporting the “manipulation over storage” explanation.

Safety/faithfulness: lower harmfulness on HEx-PHI, improving with more recurrent steps (including extrapolated steps). It also argues latent iterative traces align better with final answers than explicit CoT, suggesting less post-hoc rationalization.

Caveat: to validate the strongest headline comparisons (e.g., matching much larger models), one should check the exact benchmark suite, prompting, and aggregation in the main figures/tables.23:Tae8,技术路线分成三部分：稳定性建模、稳定架构设计、以及面向随机深度训练的算法修正。

先看建模。作者把 middle-looped 架构写成三段：prelude 单元把输入 token 映射成条件向量 e，recurrent unit 在循环步 t 上更新 hidden state h_t，coda 单元把最终状态映射到 logits。关键是把 recurrent update 视为一个关于 residual stream 的非线性时变系统，其中一部分参数控制“保留多少旧状态、注入多少新状态”。在对系统做线性化近似后，这个更新退化成经典 LTI 系统，稳定性可以用状态转移矩阵的谱性质来分析。作者发现，已有 looped 架构中的 injection 参数会学到过大的谱范数，从而导致 residual explosion。这不是经验上“有时会炸”，而是能被动力系统视角解释的结构性风险。

基于这个分析，Parcae 的核心设计是对 A 做连续到离散的稳定参数化，并把连续形式的 A 约束为 negative diagonal matrix。这样离散化后的状态更新天然带有收缩性质，谱范数被控制住，残差不会在循环中指数放大。这个设计很像把 recurrent depth 的自由度从“任意线性耦合”收缩到“逐维稳定衰减/保留”，牺牲了一部分表达灵活性，换来训练稳定性和可预测性。作者没有选择更宽松的全矩阵稳定化，而是用对角负矩阵，原因很实际：它足够稳定、参数少、实现简单，而且在大模型训练里更容易和现有 Transformer block 兼容。

除了结构约束，作者还处理了两个训练层面的尖点来源。第一，对输入条件 e 做归一化，缓解训练后期的 loss spikes。这里可以理解为 recurrent unit 在不同 loop depth 下反复接收同一个条件信号，如果其尺度漂移，容易在深循环时放大不稳定模式。第二，训练目标需要对随机深度的期望损失做优化。已有做法常在 batch 级别采样统一深度，导致梯度方差和深度切换带来的不连续更明显。Parcae 改成 intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling，让同一 batch 内不同样本走不同 loop 次数，从而平滑优化过程，也更接近“对深度分布求期望”的目标。

论文还有一个重要点是把训练时 scaling 和测试时 scaling 统一起来。训练时，他们在 isoFLOP 设定下研究给定总训练 FLOPs 时，应该把预算分给更多数据还是更多 looping；测试时，他们研究增加 loop 次数带来的 loss 改善曲线，并拟合出带 irreducible loss 的指数衰减形式。最终得到一个统一的 looping scaling 视角：训练阶段学到的 recurrent refinement 能在推理阶段继续通过更多循环释放出来，但收益遵循可预测的递减规律。24:T93b,实验分成稳定性、端到端质量、训练 FLOP scaling、测试时 scaling 四块。

稳定性方面，作者先证明旧配方确实容易出现 residual explosion 和 loss spikes，并把问题和 injection 参数的谱范数联系起来。Table 2 是关键证据之一：不稳定模型会学到更危险的 A 参数化，而 Parcae 的约束能显著抑制这种现象。文中还强调，过去一些 looped 模型往往依赖敏感超参和 Post-Norm 才能勉强收敛，Parcae 则把稳定性更多前移到参数化本身。

端到端质量方面，Parcae 与参数量、数据量匹配的 RDMs 和标准 Transformer 比较。结果上，相比 RDM，验证集 perplexity 降低 6.3%。当规模扩展到 1.3B 参数、100B tokens 时，Parcae 在 Core 和 Core-Extended benchmark 上分别比参数匹配 Transformer 高最多 2.99 和 1.18 分，并能匹配约两倍参数量的 Transformer。这是全文最重要的结果之一，因为它说明 looping 不是只在 toy setting 下省参数，而是在较实在的预训练规模上也能换到质量。

训练 FLOP scaling 方面，作者做了 parameter-matched isoFLOP 实验：总训练 FLOPs 固定时，比较把预算用于更多数据，还是用于更多 loop depth。结论是 looping 构成了与参数、数据并列的独立 scaling 轴，最优配方会同时增加数据和 looping，并满足经验幂律。Figure 1 右图是这里的核心图。这个结果的含义不是“looping 总比数据好”，而是“在固定参数下，compute-optimal 解不只是一味加数据”。

测试时 scaling 方面，作者观察到增加循环次数会带来可预测的 loss 下降，形式接近指数衰减并存在不可约下界。也就是说，模型确实学会了可继续 refinement 的动态，但额外 loop 的边际收益会越来越小。论文进一步把训练期和测试期的 scaling law 合在一起，形成统一拟合。这一点对部署很关键，因为它支持按场景做 per-token 或 per-request 的计算分配。

从全文叙述看，消融实验还覆盖了 A 的参数化方式、e normalization、以及 per-sequence depth sampling 对 loss spikes 的影响。值得注意的是，作者不是只报告最终分数，而是把训练曲线稳定性本身当成一等结果来分析，这对做大规模预训练的人更有参考价值。25:T8f4,The technical story has three parts: stability analysis, stable parameterization, and training-algorithm fixes for stochastic depth.

The model is written as a middle-looped architecture with a prelude module, a recurrent middle block, and a coda module. The recurrent update over the residual stream is cast as a nonlinear time-varying dynamical system. After linearization, the update reduces to a linear time-invariant system, which makes classical stability analysis available. The key empirical observation is that prior looped architectures can learn unstable injection operators with large spectral norms, leading to residual explosion.

Parcae addresses this by parameterizing the continuous-time state matrix A and discretizing it in a controlled way, while constraining A to be a negative diagonal matrix. This gives the recurrent update an inherently contractive character and prevents the hidden state from blowing up across loop iterations. The design is deliberately conservative: a diagonal stable parameterization gives up some flexibility relative to a full matrix, but it is simple, cheap, and robust enough for large-scale Transformer training.

The paper also identifies two practical sources of loss spikes. First, the conditioning signal e is repeatedly injected across loop steps, so scale drift in e can destabilize deep recurrence. Parcae adds normalization on e to mitigate this. Second, the training objective optimizes expected loss over variable depths. Prior recipes often sample one depth per batch, which creates higher variance and sharper optimization discontinuities. Parcae instead uses intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling, so different sequences in the same batch use different loop counts. This better matches the expectation-over-depth objective and empirically smooths training.

A further strength of the paper is that it connects training-time and inference-time scaling. Under isoFLOP training, it studies how compute should be split between more data and more looping. At test time, it studies how additional loop iterations reduce loss, finding an exponential-decay form with an irreducible floor. The result is a unified view in which recurrence learned during training can be exploited at inference, but with predictable diminishing returns.26:T98d,The experiments cover stability, end-to-end quality, training-FLOP scaling, and test-time scaling.

On stability, the paper shows that earlier looped recipes indeed suffer from residual explosion and loss spikes, and links this behavior to the learned spectral properties of the injection operator. Table 2 is central here: unstable models learn more dangerous parameterizations, while Parcae’s constrained form suppresses that failure mode. An important practical point is that prior looped models often relied on sensitive hyperparameters and normalization choices such as Post-Norm just to converge; Parcae moves much of the stability burden into the parameterization itself.

On end-to-end quality, Parcae is compared against parameter- and data-matched RDMs and standard Transformers. Relative to RDMs, it reduces validation perplexity by 6.3%. At 1.3B parameters trained on 100B tokens, it outperforms parameter-matched Transformers by up to 2.99 points on Core and 1.18 points on Core-Extended, while matching Transformers roughly twice as large. That is the headline result: looping is not only a toy parameter-saving trick, but can buy real quality at meaningful pretraining scale.

For training-FLOP scaling, the paper runs parameter-matched isoFLOP studies and asks whether extra compute should go into more data or more loop depth. The answer is that looping behaves like an additional scaling axis. FLOP-optimal training increases both data and looping according to empirical power laws. The implication is not that looping dominates data, but that under a fixed parameter budget, the compute-optimal solution is not exhausted by “just add more tokens.”

For test-time scaling, increasing the number of loop iterations yields predictable loss improvements that follow an exponential decay toward an irreducible floor. This suggests that the model learns a genuine iterative refinement process, but one with diminishing returns. The paper then combines training-time and test-time fits into a unified scaling-law view. That is especially relevant for adaptive inference and per-request compute allocation.

The ablations also examine the parameterization of A, normalization of e, and the effect of per-sequence depth sampling on loss spikes. Importantly, the paper treats training-curve stability itself as a first-class result, which makes it more useful for practitioners than papers that only report final benchmark scores.27:T5e4,This one is worth a close read. The most important part is not the benchmark table but the way the paper reformulates looped Transformers as dynamical systems and then turns that analysis into a trainable architecture.

A good reading order is: Introduction, then the formal definition of the middle-looped architecture in the background section, then the stability analysis. Pay special attention to the step from the nonlinear time-varying system to the linearized LTI view, and to why the spectral norm governs residual explosion. That is the conceptual core of the paper. After that, read the Parcae parameterization carefully: continuous A, discretization, and the negative-diagonal constraint. Then read the training fixes, especially e normalization and intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling. Several follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. The negative-diagonal parameterization is stable, but perhaps restrictive; future work could explore low-rank or block-diagonal stable forms. The exponential test-time scaling curve suggests a finite but usable reserve of iterative computation, which connects naturally to latent reasoning, adaptive compute, and early exit. Also, the choice of training-time depth distribution likely shapes the quality/compute Pareto frontier at inference. There is still room to optimize that interface.28:T7a5,The method has two main components. The first is Quantile Token Regression. Instead of predicting all quantiles from a single pooled representation, the model inserts learnable quantile tokens such as <Q_tau1> ... <Q_tauQ> directly into the input sequence. These tokens participate in self-attention together with the text tokens. Each quantile token can attend to different parts of the input and accumulate quantile-specific evidence across layers. A small regression head on top of each final quantile-token representation outputs the corresponding quantile value. The key change is architectural: the path becomes input -> quantile token interaction, rather than input -> shared representation -> separate heads. This gives each quantile a more direct route to the relevant evidence while still allowing joint modeling through shared attention.

The second component is retrieval-augmented distribution estimation. For each query, the model retrieves semantically similar neighbors from a candidate pool and appends both their texts and their empirical quantile summaries to the context. This differs from prior retrieval-based regression setups that attach only a single scalar label to each neighbor. Here, each neighbor carries a full quantile grid, so the model can observe not only central tendency but also spread and tail behavior in nearby examples. The paper positions this as local grounding for uncertainty estimation.

The loss discussion is also notable. Beyond standard quantile losses such as the pinball loss, the authors analyze what different objectives optimize under empirical-quantile supervision. That part appears more clarifying than radically new, but it helps explain why some objectives favor calibration while others favor point accuracy. Overall, the main idea is to treat structured quantile prediction as a token-level modeling problem and to extend retrieval augmentation from point prediction to distribution prediction.29:T671,The experiments use two newly constructed text-to-distribution datasets. One is based on Inside Airbnb, where the task is to predict a price distribution from listing text. The other is StackSample, derived from Stack Overflow related text and paired with a continuous target distribution. Each example has multiple observations rather than a single label, enabling empirical quantile supervision. The backbone models are Qwen3 variants ranging from 1.7B to 14B parameters.

The reported findings are straightforward. First, retrieval augmentation consistently improves quantile regression across scales: average MAPE is reduced by 8% relatively on Airbnb and by 63% on StackSample. The much larger gain on StackSample suggests that the task relies more heavily on local analogies and that the query text alone is less informative. Second, the quantile-token architecture outperforms the shared-representation baseline, with a 14% relative reduction in average MAPE on StackSample and prediction intervals that are 6x narrower. If accuracy improves while intervals become much tighter, that indicates the baseline may have been compensating for weak uncertainty modeling by producing overly diffuse estimates. Third, combining quantile tokens with neighbor context gives the best overall results, suggesting that the architectural change and retrieval grounding are complementary.

The paper also includes ablations and loss-function analysis. The most important checks when reading the full version are whether quantile crossing is explicitly handled and how the retrieval pool is constructed to avoid leakage between train and evaluation examples.2a:T782,The key idea is to treat the currently loaded expert set as an option, and to model the decision to keep or replace that set using the option-critic framework. The paper formulates dynamic expert loading as a semi-Markov decision process. The state includes context and routing-related information; the action is not a single-token expert choice but a temporally persistent expert mask; an option termination function decides when to switch; and each switch incurs a deliberation cost that stands in for real loading latency or memory movement.

Implementation-wise, each layer gets a lightweight controller. The controller learns two things: a termination policy that decides whether to continue with the current expert set, and a policy over options that selects a new set when switching happens. This differs from standard MoE routing in that routing becomes piecewise constant over spans of tokens rather than independently recomputed at every step. To avoid full retraining, the authors adapt gpt-oss-20b with only small LoRA/adapter updates plus the controller, while keeping the base model largely fixed. Training uses an option-critic style objective with a deliberation penalty, and a self-distillation reward that encourages the modified model to stay close to the original model’s behavior while learning to switch less often.

This is distinct from prior serving-side heuristics. Caching and prefetching optimize around a fixed routing distribution; expert pruning permanently reduces capacity. Here the routing policy itself is changed so the model learns to keep the current expert set whenever the expected quality gain from switching does not justify the cost. The RL analogy is clean: longer option duration yields stronger temporal coherence and easier memory management, but too much persistence reduces token-level adaptability. The deliberation cost becomes the main knob controlling that trade-off.2b:T6b3,The main experiments are built on gpt-oss-20b with a small amount of adaptation parameters. The paper first measures switching behavior in several frontier open-source MoEs and finds that active expert sets change extremely often, close to every token. On gpt-oss-20b, the baseline switch rate is above 50%, meaning the model changes expert sets roughly every other token.

With the temporally extended controller, the switch rate drops below 5%, and with stronger switching penalties it can approach 1%. On downstream evaluations such as MATH and MMLU, the adapted model retains up to about 90% of the base-model accuracy. That wording matters: the claim is not near-lossless compression of routing dynamics, but a controllable trade-off. The lower the switch rate, the more quality is sacrificed. The main empirical result is that this trade-off is learnable and tunable, rather than something that must be handled by hand-crafted heuristics.

The most important experimental pattern is likely the curve, not any single score: as deliberation cost increases, switching falls rapidly while task performance degrades more gradually. That suggests a substantial fraction of token-level routing changes in standard MoEs contribute little to final quality. If that pattern holds in larger models, longer contexts, and real offloading settings, it would matter a lot.

There are also clear limitations. The work is a post-hoc adaptation, not temporally aware MoE pretraining from scratch. And the evaluation is centered on task accuracy and switch rate, without a full end-to-end serving analysis of latency, host-device traffic, or prefetch hit rate. So the systems payoff is plausible, but not yet fully demonstrated.2c:T4f9,Start with the introduction and the problem framing. The important part is not the RL terminology, but why token-level expert churn breaks memory optimizations once experts spill beyond GPU memory. Then read the section that maps expert loading to an s-MDP. Focus on what counts as an option, what termination means in MoE terms, and how deliberation cost is injected. That is the conceptual center of the paper.

After that, go straight to the main figures and tables showing the switch-rate versus accuracy trade-off. We pre-train both models on more than 32T diverse and high-quality tokens, followed by a comprehensive post-training pipeline that unlocks and further enhances their capabilities. DeepSeek-V4-Pro- Max, the maximum reasoning effort mode of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, redefines the state-of-the-art for open models, outperforming its predecessors in core tasks. Meanwhile, DeepSeek-V4 series are highly efficient in long-context scenarios. In the one-million-token context setting, DeepSeek- V4-Pro requires only 27% of single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of KV cache compared with DeepSeek-V3.2. This enables us to routinely support one-million-token contexts, thereby making long-horizon tasks and further test-time scaling more feasible. The model checkpoints are available at https://huggingfa

DeepSeek-V4:
Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
DeepSeek-AI
research@deepseek.com
Abstract
We present a preview version of DeepSeek-V4 series, including two strong Mixture-of-
Experts (MoE) language models — DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated) and
DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated) — both supporting a context length of
one million tokens. DeepSeek-V4 series incorporate several key upgrades in architecture and op-
timization: (1) a hybrid attention architecture that combines Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA)
and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) to improve long-context efficiency; (2) Manifold-
Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) that enhance conventional residual connections; (3)
and the Muon optimizer for faster convergence and greater training stability. We pre-train
both models on more than 32T diverse and high-quality tokens, followed by a comprehensive
post-training pipeline that unlocks and further enhances their capabilities. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-
Max, the maximum reasoning effort mode of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, redefines the state-of-the-art for
open models, outperforming its predecessors in core tasks. Meanwhile, DeepSeek-V4 series are
highly efficient in long-context scenarios. In the one-million-token context setting, DeepSeek-
V4-Pro requires only 27% of single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of KV cache compared
with DeepSeek-V3.2. This enables us to routinely support one-million-token contexts, thereby
making long-horizon tasks and further test-time scaling more feasible. The model checkpoints
are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.

1. Introduction
The emergence of reasoning models (DeepSeek-AI, 2025; OpenAI, 2024c) has established a
new paradigm of test-time scaling, driving substantial performance gains for Large Language
Models (LLMs). However, this scaling paradigm is fundamentally constrained by the quadratic
computational complexity of the vanilla attention mechanism (Vaswani et al., 2017), which
creates a prohibitive bottleneck for ultra-long contexts and reasoning processes. Concurrently,
the emergence of long-horizon scenarios and tasks — from complex agentic workflows to
massive cross-document analysis — has also made efficient support for ultra-long contexts
critical for future progress. While recent open-source efforts (Bai et al., 2025a; DeepSeek-AI,
2024; MiniMax, 2025; Qwen, 2025) have advanced general capabilities, this core architectural
inefficiency in handling ultra-long sequences remains a key impediment, limiting further gains
from test-time scaling and hindering further exploration into long-horizon scenarios and tasks.
In order to break the efficiency barrier in ultra-long contexts, we develop the DeepSeek-V4
series, including the preview versions of DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated)
and DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated). Through architectural innova-
tions, DeepSeek-V4 series achieve a dramatic leap in computational efficiency for processing
ultra-long sequences. This breakthrough enables efficient support for a context length of one
million tokens, ushering in a new era of million-length contexts for next-generation LLMs. We
believe our capability to efficiently handle ultra-long sequences unlocks the next frontier of
test-time scaling, paves the way for deeper research into long-horizon tasks, and establishes a
necessary foundation for exploring future paradigms like online learning.
Compared with the DeepSeek-V3 architecture (DeepSeek-AI, 2024), DeepSeek-V4 series
retain the DeepSeekMoE framework (Dai et al., 2024) and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) strategy,
while introducing several key innovations in architecture and optimization. To enhance long-
context efficiency, we design a hybrid attention mechanism combining Compressed Sparse
Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA). CSA compresses the KV caches
along the sequence dimension and then performs DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) (DeepSeek-
AI, 2025), whereas HCA applies more aggressive compression to the KV caches but keeps
dense attention. To strengthen modeling capability, we incorporate Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) that upgrade conventional residual connections.
Additionally, we introduce the Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) optimizer to the
training of DeepSeek-V4 series, leading to faster convergence and improved training stability.
To enable efficient training and inference for DeepSeek-V4 series as well as productive de-
velopment, we introduce several infrastructure optimizations. First, we design and implement
a single fused kernel for MoE modules that fully overlaps computation, communication, and
memory access. Second, we employ TileLang (Wang et al., 2026), a Domain-Specific Language
(DSL) to balance development productivity and runtime efficiency. Third, we provide efficient
batch-invariant and deterministic kernel libraries to ensure bitwise reproducibility across train-
ing and inference. Fourth, we incorporate FP4 quantization-aware training for MoE expert
weights and the indexer QK path to reduce memory and computation. Fifth, for the training
framework, we extend the autograd framework with tensor-level checkpointing for fine-grained
recomputation control; and we enhance training efficiency with a hybrid ZeRO strategy for the
Muon optimizer, cost-effective mHC implementations via recomputation and fused kernels, and
two-stage contextual parallelism to manage compressed attention. Finally, for the inference
framework, we design a heterogeneous KV cache structure with on-disk storage strategies to
enable efficient shared-prefix reuse.
4

By employing hybrid CSA and HCA, along with precision optimizations on computation
and storage, DeepSeek-V4 series achieve significantly lower inference FLOPs and a substantially
reduced KV cache size compared with DeepSeek-V3.2, especially in long-context settings. The
right part of Figure 1 demonstrates the estimated single-token inference FLOPs and accumulated
KV cache size of DeepSeek-V3.2 and DeepSeek-V4 series. In the scenario of 1M-token context,
even DeepSeek-V4-Pro, which has a larger number of activated parameters, attains only 27%
of the single-token FLOPs (measured in equivalent FP8 FLOPs) and 10% of the KV cache
size relative to DeepSeek-V3.2. Furthermore, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with its smaller number of
activated parameters, pushes efficiency even further: in the 1M-token context setting, it achieves
only 10% of the single-token FLOPs and 7% of the KV cache size compared with DeepSeek-V3.2.
Additionally, for DeepSeek-V4 series, the routed expert parameters utilize FP4 precision. While
the peak FLOPs for FP4 × FP8 operations are currently the same as FP8 × FP8 on existing
hardware, they can theoretically be implemented to be 1/3 more efficient on future hardware,
which will further enhance the efficiency of DeepSeek-V4 series.
During pre-training, we train DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 32T tokens and DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 33T
tokens, respectively. After pre-training, these two models can natively and efficiently support
1M-length contexts. In our internal evaluations, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base already surpasses
DeepSeek-V3.2-Base across a majority of benchmarks with its more parameter-efficient design.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base further extends this advantage to set a new performance standard among
DeepSeek foundation models, achieving comprehensive superiority across reasoning, coding,
long-context, and world knowledge tasks.
The post-training pipeline of DeepSeek-V4 series features a two-stage paradigm: the inde-
pendent cultivation of domain-specific experts, followed by unified model consolidation via
on-policy distillation (Lu and Lab, 2025). Initially, for each target domain — such as mathematics,
coding, agent, and instruction following — a separate expert model is trained independently.
The base model first undergoes Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on high-quality, domain-specific
data to establish foundational capabilities. Subsequently, Reinforcement Learning (RL) is ap-
plied using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (DeepSeek-AI, 2025), which further
optimizes the model for domain-aligned behaviors guided by reward models tailored to specific
success criteria. This phase yields a diverse set of specialized experts, each excelling in its
respective field. Finally, to integrate these distinct proficiencies, a single unified model is trained
through on-policy distillation, wherein the unified model acts as the student learning to optimize
the reverse KL loss with teacher models.
Summary of Core Evaluation Results
• Knowledge: In assessments of broad world knowledge, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max, the maxi-
mum reasoning effort mode of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, significantly outperforms leading open-
source models on the SimpleQA (OpenAI, 2024d) and Chinese-SimpleQA (He et al., 2024)
benchmarks. Regarding educational knowledge — evaluated via MMLU-Pro (Wang et al.,
2024b), HLE (Phan et al., 2025), and GPQA (Rein et al., 2023) — DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max
shows a marginal lead over its open-source counterparts. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max has
significantly closed the gap with the leading proprietary model, Gemini-3.1-Pro, despite
still trailing it in these knowledge-based evaluations.
• Reasoning: Through the expansion of reasoning tokens, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max demon-
strates superior performance relative to GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3.0-Pro on standard reasoning
benchmarks. Nevertheless, its performance falls marginally short of GPT-5.4 and Gemini-
3.1-Pro, suggesting a developmental trajectory that trails state-of-the-art frontier models by
approximately 3 to 6 months. Furthermore, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Max achieves comparable

• Agent: On public benchmarks, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max is on par with leading open-source

get. In agent evaluations, while DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Max matches the performance of
DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max on several benchmarks, it still trails its larger counterpart on more
complex, high-difficulty tasks.
2. Architecture
Overall, DeepSeek-V4 series retain the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) architecture and Multi-
Token Prediction (MTP) modules (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; Gloeckle et al., 2024), while introducing
several key upgrades over DeepSeek-V3: (1) firstly, we introduce the Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) to strengthen conventional residual connections;
6

(2) secondly, we design a hybrid attention architecture, which greatly improves long-context
efficiency through Compressed Sparse Attention and Heavily Compressed Attention. (3) thirdly,
we employ Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) as the optimizer. For the Mixture-of-
Experts (MoE) components, we still adopt the DeepSeekMoE (Dai et al., 2024) architecture, with
only minor adjustments from DeepSeek-V3. The Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) (DeepSeek-AI,
2024; Gloeckle et al., 2024; Li et al., 2024; Qi et al., 2020) configuration remains identical to
that of DeepSeek-V3. All other unspecified details follow the settings established in DeepSeek-
V3 (DeepSeek-AI, 2024). Figure 2 illustrates the overall architecture of DeepSeek-V4, and the
details are described below.
2.1. Designs Inherited from DeepSeek-V3
Mixture-of-Experts.
As previous DeepSeek-series models (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; DeepSeek-AI,
2024), DeepSeek-V4 series also adopt the DeepSeekMoE paradigm (Dai et al., 2024) for Feed-
Forward Networks (FFNs), which sets fine-grained routed experts and shared experts. Different
from DeepSeek-V3, we change the activation function that computes the affinity scores from
Sigmoid(·) into Sqrt(Softplus(·)). For load balancing, we also employ the auxiliary-loss-free
strategy (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; Wang et al., 2024a), augmented by a slight sequence-wise balance
loss that prevents extreme imbalance within individual sequences. For DeepSeek-V4, we remove
the constraint on the number of routing target nodes, and carefully redesign the parallelism
strategy to maintain training efficiency. Furthermore, compared with DeepSeek-V3, we replace
the dense FFN layers in the initial several Transformer blocks with MoE layers that employ
Hash routing (Roller et al., 2021). The Hash routing strategy determines the target experts of
each token according to a predefined hash function with regard to the input token ID.
Multi-Token Prediction.
As DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-V4 series also set MTP modules and
objectives. Given that the MTP strategy has been validated in DeepSeek-V3, we adopt the same
strategy for DeepSeek-V4 series without modification.
2.2. Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
As shown in Figure 2, DeepSeek-V4 series incorporate Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
(mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) to strengthen the conventional residual connections between adjacent
Transformer blocks. Compared with naive Hyper-Connections (HC) (Zhu et al., 2025), the core
idea of mHC is to constrain the residual mapping onto a specific manifold, and thus enhance the
stability of signal propagation across layers while preserving model expressivity. This subsection
briefly introduces the standard HC and describes how we design mHC for stable training.
Standard Hyper-Connections.
The standard HC expands the width of the residual

1. Introduction
The emergence of reasoning models (DeepSeek-AI, 2025; OpenAI, 2024c) has established a
new paradigm of test-time scaling, driving substantial performance gains for Large Language
Models (LLMs). However, this scaling paradigm is fundamentally constrained by the quadratic
computational complexity of the vanilla attention mechanism (Vaswani et al., 2017), which
creates a prohibitive bottleneck for ultra-long contexts and reasoning processes. Concurrently,
the emergence of long-horizon scenarios and tasks — from complex agentic workflows to
massive cross-document analysis — has also made efficient support for ultra-long contexts
critical for future progress. While recent open-source efforts (Bai et al., 2025a; DeepSeek-AI,
2024; MiniMax, 2025; Qwen, 2025) have advanced general capabilities, this core architectural
inefficiency in handling ultra-long sequences remains a key impediment, limiting further gains
from test-time scaling and hindering further exploration into long-horizon scenarios and tasks.
In order to break the efficiency barrier in ultra-long contexts, we develop the DeepSeek-V4
series, including the preview versions of DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated)
and DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated). Through architectural innova-
tions, DeepSeek-V4 series achieve a dramatic leap in computational efficiency for processing
ultra-long sequences. This breakthrough enables efficient support for a context length of one
million tokens, ushering in a new era of million-length contexts for next-generation LLMs. We
believe our capability to efficiently handle ultra-long sequences unlocks the next frontier of
test-time scaling, paves the way for deeper research into long-horizon tasks, and establishes a
necessary foundation for exploring future paradigms like online learning.
Compared with the DeepSeek-V3 architecture (DeepSeek-AI, 2024), DeepSeek-V4 series
retain the DeepSeekMoE framework (Dai et al., 2024) and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) strategy,
while introducing several key innovations in architecture and optimization. To enhance long-
context efficiency, we design a hybrid attention mechanism combining Compressed Sparse
Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA). CSA compresses the KV caches
along the sequence dimension and then performs DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) (DeepSeek-
AI, 2025), whereas HCA applies more aggressive compression to the KV caches but keeps
dense attention. To strengthen modeling capability, we incorporate Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) that upgrade conventional residual connections.
Additionally, we introduce the Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) optimizer to the
training of DeepSeek-V4 series, leading to faster convergence and improved training stability.
To enable efficient training and inference for DeepSeek-V4 series as well as productive de-
velopment, we introduce several infrastructure optimizations. First, we design and implement
a single fused kernel for MoE modules that fully overlaps computation, communication, and
memory access. Second, we employ TileLang (Wang et al., 2026), a Domain-Specific Language
(DSL) to balance development productivity and runtime efficiency. Third, we provide efficient
batch-invariant and deterministic kernel libraries to ensure bitwise reproducibility across train-
ing and inference. Fourth, we incorporate FP4 quantization-aware training for MoE expert
weights and the indexer QK path to reduce memory and computation. Fifth, for the training
framework, we extend the autograd framework with tensor-level checkpointing for fine-grained
recomputation control; and we enhance training efficiency with a hybrid ZeRO strategy for the
Muon optimizer, cost-effective mHC implementations via recomputation and fused kernels, and
two-stage contextual parallelism to manage compressed attention. Finally, for the inference
framework, we design a heterogeneous KV cache structure with on-disk storage strategies to
enable efficient shared-prefix reuse.
4

By employing hybrid CSA and HCA, along with precision optimizations on computation
and storage, DeepSeek-V4 series achieve significantly lower inference FLOPs and a substantially
reduced KV cache size compared with DeepSeek-V3.2, especially in long-context settings. The
right part of Figure 1 demonstrates the estimated single-token inference FLOPs and accumulated
KV cache size of DeepSeek-V3.2 and DeepSeek-V4 series. In the scenario of 1M-token context,
even DeepSeek-V4-Pro, which has a larger number of activated parameters, attains only 27%
of the single-token FLOPs (measured in equivalent FP8 FLOPs) and 10% of the KV cache
size relative to DeepSeek-V3.2. Furthermore, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with its smaller number of
activated parameters, pushes efficiency even further: in the 1M-token context setting, it achieves
only 10% of the single-token FLOPs and 7% of the KV cache size compared with DeepSeek-V3.2.
Additionally, for DeepSeek-V4 series, the routed expert parameters utilize FP4 precision. While
the peak FLOPs for FP4 × FP8 operations are currently the same as FP8 × FP8 on existing
hardware, they can theoretically be implemented to be 1/3 more efficient on future hardware,
which will further enhance the efficiency of DeepSeek-V4 series.
During pre-training, we train DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 32T tokens and DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 33T
tokens, respectively. After pre-training, these two models can natively and efficiently support
1M-length contexts. In our internal evaluations, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base already surpasses
DeepSeek-V3.2-Base across a majority of benchmarks with its more parameter-efficient design.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base further extends this advantage to set a new performance standard among
DeepSeek foundation models, achieving comprehensive superiority across reasoning, coding,
long-context, and world knowledge tasks.
The post-training pipeline of DeepSeek-V4 series features a two-stage paradigm: the inde-
pendent cultivation of domain-specific experts, followed by unified model consolidation via
on-policy distillation (Lu and Lab, 2025). Initially, for each target domain — such as mathematics,
coding, agent, and instruction following — a separate expert model is trained independently.
The base model first undergoes Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on high-quality, domain-specific
data to establish foundational capabilities. Subsequently, Reinforcement Learning (RL) is ap-
plied using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (DeepSeek-AI, 2025), which further
optimizes the model for domain-aligned behaviors guided by reward models tailored to specific
success criteria. This phase yields a diverse set of specialized experts, each excelling in its
respective field. Finally, to integrate these distinct proficiencies, a single unified model is trained
through on-policy distillation, wherein the unified model acts as the student learning to optimize
the reverse KL loss with teacher models.
Summary of Core Evaluation Results
• Knowledge: In assessments of broad world knowledge, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max, the maxi-
mum reasoning effort mode of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, significantly outperforms leading open-
source models on the SimpleQA (OpenAI, 2024d) and Chinese-SimpleQA (He et al., 2024)
benchmarks. Regarding educational knowledge — evaluated via MMLU-Pro (Wang et al.,
2024b), HLE (Phan et al., 2025), and GPQA (Rein et al., 2023) — DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max
shows a marginal lead over its open-source counterparts. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max has
significantly closed the gap with the leading proprietary model, Gemini-3.1-Pro, despite
still trailing it in these knowledge-based evaluations.
• Reasoning: Through the expansion of reasoning tokens, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max demon-
strates superior performance relative to GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3.0-Pro on standard reasoning
benchmarks. Nevertheless, its performance falls marginally short of GPT-5.4 and Gemini-
3.1-Pro, suggesting a developmental trajectory that trails state-of-the-art frontier models by
approximately 3 to 6 months. Furthermore, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Max achieves comparable

DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max on several benchmarks, it still trails its larger counterpart on more
complex, high-difficulty tasks.
2. Architecture
Overall, DeepSeek-V4 series retain the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) architecture and Multi-
Token Prediction (MTP) modules (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; Gloeckle et al., 2024), while introducing
several key upgrades over DeepSeek-V3: (1) firstly, we introduce the Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) to strengthen conventional residual connections;
6

(2) secondly, we design a hybrid attention architecture, which greatly improves long-context
efficiency through Compressed Sparse Attention and Heavily Compressed Attention. (3) thirdly,
we employ Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) as the optimizer. For the Mixture-of-
Experts (MoE) components, we still adopt the DeepSeekMoE (Dai et al., 2024) architecture, with
only minor adjustments from DeepSeek-V3. The Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) (DeepSeek-AI,
2024; Gloeckle et al., 2024; Li et al., 2024; Qi et al., 2020) configuration remains identical to
that of DeepSeek-V3. All other unspecified details follow the settings established in DeepSeek-
V3 (DeepSeek-AI, 2024). Figure 2 illustrates the overall architecture of DeepSeek-V4, and the
details are described below.
2.1. Designs Inherited from DeepSeek-V3
Mixture-of-Experts.
As previous DeepSeek-series models (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; DeepSeek-AI,
2024), DeepSeek-V4 series also adopt the DeepSeekMoE paradigm (Dai et al., 2024) for Feed-
Forward Networks (FFNs), which sets fine-grained routed experts and shared experts. Different
from DeepSeek-V3, we change the activation function that computes the affinity scores from
Sigmoid(·) into Sqrt(Softplus(·)). For load balancing, we also employ the auxiliary-loss-free
strategy (DeepSeek-AI, 2024; Wang et al., 2024a), augmented by a slight sequence-wise balance
loss that prevents extreme imbalance within individual sequences. For DeepSeek-V4, we remove
the constraint on the number of routing target nodes, and carefully redesign the parallelism
strategy to maintain training efficiency. Furthermore, compared with DeepSeek-V3, we replace
the dense FFN layers in the initial several Transformer blocks with MoE layers that employ
Hash routing (Roller et al., 2021). The Hash routing strategy determines the target experts of
each token according to a predefined hash function with regard to the input token ID.
Multi-Token Prediction.
As DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-V4 series also set MTP modules and
objectives. Given that the MTP strategy has been validated in DeepSeek-V3, we adopt the same
strategy for DeepSeek-V4 series without modification.
2.2. Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
As shown in Figure 2, DeepSeek-V4 series incorporate Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
(mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) to strengthen the conventional residual connections between adjacent
Transformer blocks. Compared with naive Hyper-Connections (HC) (Zhu et al., 2025), the core
idea of mHC is to constrain the residual mapping onto a specific manifold, and thus enhance the
stability of signal propagation across layers while preserving model expressivity. This subsection
briefly introduces the standard HC and describes how we design mHC for stable training.
Standard Hyper-Connections.
The standard HC expands the width of the residual stream
by a factor of 𝑛hc. Specifically, the shape of the residual stream is expanded from R𝑑to R𝑛hc×𝑑,
where 𝑑is the hidden size of the actual layer input. Let 𝑋𝑙= [x𝑙,1; . . . ; x𝑙,𝑛hc]𝑇∈R𝑛hc×𝑑be the
residual state before the 𝑙-th layer. HC introduces three linear mappings: an input mapping
𝐴𝑙∈R1×𝑛hc, a residual transformation 𝐵𝑙∈R𝑛hc×𝑛hc, and an output mapping 𝐶𝑙∈R𝑛hc×1. The
update of the residual state is then formulated as:
𝑋𝑙+1 = 𝐵𝑙𝑋𝑙+ 𝐶𝑙F𝑙(𝐴𝑙𝑋𝑙),
(1)
where F𝑙denotes the 𝑙-th layer (e.g., an MoE layer), whose input and output shapes are both
R𝑑. Note that the actual layer input 𝐴𝑙𝑋𝑙∈R𝑑is also 𝑑-dimensional, so the expanded residual
7

width does not influence the design of the inner layers. HC decouples the residual width from
the actual hidden size, offering a complementary scaling axis with minimal computational
overhead, as 𝑛hc is typically much smaller than the hidden size 𝑑. However, even though HC
has demonstrated potential in improving model performance, we find that the training will
frequently exhibit numerical instability when stacking multiple layers, which hinders the scaling
of HC.
Manifold-Constrained Residual Mapping.
The core innovation of mHC is to constrain the
residual mapping matrix 𝐵𝑙to the manifold of doubly stochastic matrices (the Birkhoff polytope)
M, and thus enhance the stability of signal propagation across layers:
𝐵𝑙∈M ≔{𝑀∈R𝑛×𝑛| 𝑀1𝑛= 1𝑛, 1𝑇
𝑛𝑀= 1𝑇
𝑛, 𝑀⩾0}.
(2)
This constraint ensures that the spectral norm of the mapping matrix ∥𝐵𝑙∥2 is bounded by 1, so
the residual transformation is non-expansive, which increases the numerical stability during both
the forward pass and backpropagation. Besides, the set M is closed under multiplication, which
guarantees stability in the scenarios of deep stacks of mHC. In addition, the input transformation
𝐴𝑙and output transformation 𝐶𝑙are also constrained to be non-negative and bounded via a
Sigmoid function to avoid the risk of signal cancellation.

2.3. Hybrid Attention with CSA and HCA
As the context length reaches extreme scales, the attention mechanism emerges as the dominant
computational bottleneck in a model. For DeepSeek-V4, we design two efficient attention
architectures — Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA)
— and employ their interleaved hybrid configuration, which substantially reduces the compu-
tational cost of attention in long-text scenarios. CSA integrates both compression and sparse
attention strategies: it first compresses the Key-Value (KV) cache of every 𝑚tokens into one
entry, and then applies DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) (DeepSeek-AI, 2025) where each query
token attends to only 𝑘compressed KV entries. HCA aims for extreme compression by consol-
idating the KV cache of every 𝑚′ (≫𝑚) tokens into a single entry. The hybrid architecture of
CSA and HCA remarkably improves the long-context efficiency of DeepSeek-V4 series, making
one-million-token context feasible in practice. This subsection describes the core techniques
of our hybrid attention architecture, and we also provide an open-source implementation1 to
specify more details unambiguously.
